sources.entry: CC-Switch - A cross-platform desktop All-in-One assistant for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and AI coding agents. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: CC Switch is a cross-platform desktop app that manages API providers, MCP servers, Skills, and prompts across AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode from one interface.
summary.what_it_does: The app lets you add API provider presets (90+ listed) or custom configs and switch between them in one click, replacing only the endpoint, key, and model in each tool's config file. It provides a unified panel for MCP servers, Skills, and per-tool prompt files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md) that can be synced to the supported tools. Local routing forwards requests on your machine, converting between Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini API formats, with auto-failover through a provider queue. Aggregation mode puts models from several providers into one model list in Claude Code or Codex. It also includes a session reading view, usage and quota tracking, and cloud sync via WebDAV or S3-compatible storage.
use_cases: switch API providers for Claude Code or Codex
use GPT models inside Claude Code
manage MCP servers across multiple AI coding tools
track token usage and spending for AI coding agents
browse and resume AI coding session history
sync AI tool configuration across devices
how_to_run: Download .msi or portable .zip from the Releases page (Windows)
Download .dmg or .zip from the Releases page (macOS)
Download .deb, .rpm, or .AppImage from the Releases page (Linux)
notable: Manages twelve AI coding tools, including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Hermes, from one desktop app
Local routing converts between Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions/Responses, and Gemini Native formats
Aggregation mode shows models from several providers in one client model picker
Preserves user-added plugins, hooks, MCP, and comments when switching configs
Session reading view summarizes each turn's steps, changed files, and failures
caveats: Linux requires glibc 2.35+ and WebKitGTK 4.1; RHEL, Rocky, and Alma 8–9 are not supported yet
Flatpak is not in official releases and must be built from the .deb
Using subscriptions through Accounts outside the official client may violate vendor terms of service, as the README warns
Much of the README is sponsor content; the README itself is long and includes many paid third-party relay promotions
